episode_summary: Hashing It Out interview (Nov 2023) with Ameen Soleimani, co-author of the Privacy Pools paper. He explains why Tornado Cash was sanctioned, how association sets and zero-knowledge inclusion and exclusion proofs let users prove their funds are not from illicit sources, the one-week analytics delay, relayers and coordination problems, and the prosecutions of Tornado Cash developers. The hosts push back on whether it weakens privacy and on the wider compliance trade-off.

cards.claim: In November 2023 a host said North Korea was laundering roughly 620 to 630 million dollars taken in the Axie Infinity hack, trying any medium possible.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they're trying to use you know any medium possible in order to launder the funds that you know they got through the hack of axi infinity

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said OFAC and other US regulators had sanctioned Tornado Cash.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: the instantiation of Tornado Cash was sanctioned by OFAC and other US regulatory bodies.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani explained that Tornado Cash was sanctioned as a whole because users had no way to prove their deposits were not illicit.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: There was no way to prove that my funds that I participated in Tornado Cash were not a part of the illicit funds.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani described zero-knowledge proofs as revealing only the information needed to prove group membership, such as being in or out of a group.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: which only discloses the amount of information that's required to prove a certain claim, namely, I'm in this group or I'm not in this group.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said Zcash was the first zk-STARK deployment in human history and Tornado Cash the second to reach production.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: Zcash was the first ever ZKStarks deployment in human history. TornadoCash was the second one to hit prop.

cards.claim: In November 2023 the hosts and Ameen Soleimani argued that privacy is not all or nothing, and that zero-knowledge proofs allow selective disclosure in between.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: what people most most people think about privacy is that it's either all or nothing

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said that 100 million dollars leaving a DeFi protocol quickly is probably not legitimate, and that such funds should be excluded.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: 100 million dollars leaves a DeFi protocol real fast it's probably not legit

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said Privacy Pools waits one week before a deposit joins the association set, a figure picked because analytics firms need three or four days to trace funds.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: after the end of a week, that's sort of a number that we picked based on how long it takes them to do this analysis.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said anyone who used Tornado Cash in full violation of sanctions law faced up to 20 years in prison.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: you're welcome to use tornado cash as is uh in full violation of sanctions law and face up to 20 years in prison

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said the association set could be any group, such as only the people KYC'd by banks, with the rules left to governments and regulators.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: it's set up to be flexible the association set can be anything being just the not terrorists it could be only the people kyc to banks right

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani argued that building a new private layer one would not solve his problem, because Ethereum is public and not going anywhere.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: building a new private L one is like not going to solve my problem

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said he would back base-layer privacy only if provable dissociation were built into the base layer as well.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: And people are like, we should do base layer privacy. And I'm like, maybe, But only if we can also do the provable dissociation of the base layer too.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said he wanted to dissociate from known criminals such as North Korean hackers and the IRGC, which would otherwise be able to use Tornado Cash.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: But I'm sure that if the North Koreans can figure out tornado cash, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani predicted people would more or less figure out the coordination problem of agreeing on which association sets count as legitimate.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: I think people will more or less figure this one out.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said that revealing any additional information weakens privacy guarantees, so Privacy Pools trades some privacy for the ability to dissociate from illicit funds.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: Will it weaken privacy? Yes, is the short answer to that.

cards.claim: In November 2023 a host said that so far in 2023, about 250 million dollars had been stolen from DeFi hacks.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: so far, $250 million have been stolen in 2023 from DeFi hacks.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said the Privacy Pools demo had been live for six months on Optimism.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: so we have a demo it's been live throughout six months on optimism

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani recounted that someone bridged ETH withdrawn from a Tornado Cash pool into the Privacy Pools demo, and he tweeted asking for those deposits to be excluded.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: Somebody bridged ETH that they withdrew out of the Gourley tornado cache up into the Optimism Gourley bridge.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani explained that a relayer pays gas for a fresh address and is paid a small fee from the withdrawal, which avoids a chicken-and-egg problem.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: so to solve that there's a relayer and so the relayer is authorized to take a small amount of your withdrawal

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani proposed that a consortium of banks could share one association set of all KYC'd deposits, so customers could withdraw without revealing their bank.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: imagine if there was a consortium of banks and they worked together on the association set and the association set was like all KYC deposits across all of our banks

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said the world of privacy was seen as bad and criminal, and that positive use cases needed to shatter that narrative.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: And so right now we're living in the privacy is bad and criminals want it world of privacy. And I think we need to shatter that.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said Tornado Cash was not a mistake but an important stepping stone, and that the mistake was not building and advertising the compliance tool fast enough.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: I don't think TornadoCache was a mistake. I think it was an important stepping stone to get here.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said Tornado Cash developer Alexei Pertsev (transcribed as Perseff) was held without bail in a Netherlands jail for nine months and was awaiting trial in March.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: Alexei Perseff was thrown in a Netherlands jail. He was held without bail for nine months.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said Tornado Cash co-founder Roman Storm was arrested in the United States about three weeks earlier and charged with money laundering.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: about three weeks ago Roman Storm got arrested in the United States and he was also charged with money laundering and such

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said Roman Semenov was on the US sanctions list, which he called preposterous for an open source developer.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: In the case of Seminov, he's sanctioned by the U.S. government.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani argued that the Tornado Cash smart contracts were immutable and its website hosted on IPFS, so the developers could not have shut out bad actors.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: the smart contracts were immutable, even if they shut everything down. Their website, even the website was hosted on IPFS and stuff.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said that anyone building privacy tools should assume malicious actors will use them.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: you should assume that if you build something like this, malicious actors will show up and use it.

cards.claim: Ameen Soleimani said privacy tools should give users the means to dissociate from bad actors so they are not forced to associate with them.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: give your own users the tools to dissociate from them so that they're not forced to associate with them if they want to have some degree of privacy.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani gave the trademark one-liner for Privacy Pools as I'm not the bad guys, here's proof.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: I'm not the bad guys. Here's proof.

cards.claim: A host explained that the paper's equilibrium means the total pool of funds naturally splits into funds that associate with a set and funds that do not.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: equilibrium using that paper is like this interesting concept where the total pool of funds naturally emerges into two groups.

cards.claim: In November 2023 Ameen Soleimani said privacy is a means to optionality in a more generalised system, so privacy belongs at lower layers.
cards.speaker: Ameen Soleimani
cards.quote: I think that's the claim that I try to push forward is that privacy is a means for optionality in a more generalized system.

title: Ameen Soleimani of Privacy Pools | Unpacking Privacy Pools – Motivations, Mechanics, and Tradeoffs
